title: Sleep and teenagers
script: Narrator: Many teenagers find it difficult to wake up early for school. Scientists say that this is not simply laziness. During adolescence, the body's internal clock shifts, so teenagers naturally feel sleepy later at night. As a result, some schools in the United States have moved their start times from around seven thirty to after eight thirty. Studies found that students at these schools slept longer, were absent less often, and had better grades. However, some parents complained that later start times made it harder to arrange transportation and after-school activities.
translation: 多くの10代の若者は、学校のために早起きするのが難しいと感じている。科学者によれば、これは単なる怠けではない。思春期には体内時計がずれるため、10代は自然と夜遅くに眠くなる。その結果、米国の一部の学校は始業時間を7時半ごろから8時半以降に遅らせた。研究によると、こうした学校の生徒は睡眠時間が長くなり、欠席が減り、成績も上がった。しかし、始業が遅いと送迎や放課後の活動の調整が難しくなると不満を言う保護者もいた。

questions.question: Why do teenagers find it hard to wake up early?
choices: Their internal clocks shift during adolescence.
They spend too much time using smartphones.
They do not get enough exercise.
Their schools start later than before.
questions.explanation: 思春期には体内時計がずれて自然と夜遅くに眠くなる、と説明されている。単なる怠けではないとも述べている。

questions.question: What was one problem with later school start times?
choices: Some parents found transportation harder to arrange.
Students' grades became worse.
Students were absent more often.
Teachers had to work longer hours.
questions.explanation: 最後に、送迎や放課後の活動の調整が難しくなると不満を言う保護者がいたとある。成績や欠席はむしろ改善した。

title: Cargo ships with sails
script: Narrator: Shipping is responsible for about three percent of global greenhouse gas emissions. To reduce this, some companies are returning to an old technology: sails. Modern cargo ships are being fitted with large, hard sails or spinning metal cylinders that use the wind to push the ship forward. Tests have shown that these devices can cut fuel use by up to twenty percent on some routes. However, the sails are expensive to install, and they work best on routes with strong, steady winds, so they cannot completely replace engines.
translation: 海運は世界の温室効果ガス排出量の約3%を占めている。これを減らすため、昔の技術である帆に立ち返る企業がある。現代の貨物船に、風を使って船を前に進める大きく硬い帆や回転する金属の円筒が取り付けられている。試験では、航路によっては燃料の使用を最大20%減らせることが示された。しかし帆は取り付け費用が高く、強く安定した風が吹く航路で最も効果を発揮するため、エンジンに完全に取って代わることはできない。

questions.question: What have tests shown about the new sails?
choices: They allow ships to travel twice as fast.
They work best when there is no wind.
They can reduce fuel use on some routes.
They have replaced engines on most ships.
questions.explanation: 航路によっては燃料の使用を最大20%減らせると述べている。

questions.question: What is one limitation of the sails?
choices: They make ships more dangerous.
They are costly to install.
They can only be used on small ships.
They increase greenhouse gas emissions.
questions.explanation: 取り付け費用が高く、強く安定した風の航路でしか最も効果がないとある。

title: The benefits of boredom
script: Narrator: Today, many people reach for their smartphones the moment they feel bored. However, some psychologists believe that boredom can actually be useful. In one study, participants who first completed a dull task, such as copying numbers from a phone book, later came up with more creative ideas than those who did not. Researchers think that when we are bored, our minds begin to wander, and this allows us to make unexpected connections. They suggest that people, especially children, should sometimes be allowed to feel bored instead of being constantly entertained.
translation: 今日、多くの人は退屈を感じた瞬間にスマートフォンに手を伸ばす。しかし、退屈は実は役に立つと考える心理学者もいる。ある研究では、電話帳の番号を書き写すような退屈な作業を先にした参加者は、そうしなかった参加者より後で創造的なアイデアを多く出した。退屈すると心がさまよい始め、それによって思いがけない結びつきが生まれるのだと研究者は考えている。人々、特に子どもには、絶えず楽しませるのではなく、ときには退屈させてもよいと彼らは提案している。

questions.question: What did the study find?
choices: People who did a boring task later had more creative ideas.
People who used smartphones were less bored.
Copying numbers improved people's memory.
Children are more easily bored than adults.
questions.explanation: 退屈な作業を先にした参加者のほうが後で創造的なアイデアを多く出したとある。

questions.question: What do the researchers suggest?
choices: People should avoid boring tasks at work.
Parents should give children more smartphones.
Children should sometimes be allowed to feel bored.
Schools should teach children to copy numbers.
questions.explanation: 最後に、特に子どもはときには退屈させてもよいと提案している。

title: Glass recycling problems
script: Narrator: Glass can be recycled again and again without losing quality, so it may seem like an ideal material. In reality, however, much of the glass that people put in recycling bins is never recycled. One reason is that glass often breaks during collection and becomes mixed with other materials, making it difficult to sort. In addition, glass is heavy, so transporting it to recycling plants is expensive. To solve these problems, some towns now collect glass separately from other recyclables and have built recycling facilities closer to where people live.
translation: ガラスは品質を落とさずに何度でもリサイクルできるので、理想的な素材に思えるかもしれない。しかし実際には、人々がリサイクル箱に入れるガラスの多くはリサイクルされていない。理由の一つは、回収中にガラスが割れてほかの素材と混ざり、分別が難しくなることだ。さらにガラスは重いので、リサイクル工場へ運ぶ費用が高い。こうした問題を解決するため、一部の町ではほかの資源ごみと分けてガラスを回収し、住民の近くにリサイクル施設を建てている。

questions.question: Why is much glass not recycled?
choices: It loses quality each time it is recycled.
People rarely put glass in recycling bins.
It breaks and becomes mixed with other materials.
Recycling plants refuse to accept colored glass.
questions.explanation: 回収中に割れてほかの素材と混ざり分別が難しくなる、と説明されている。品質は落ちないとあるので2つ目は誤り。

questions.question: What have some towns done?
choices: Stopped collecting glass completely.
Collected glass separately and built facilities nearby.
Asked people to reuse glass bottles at home.
Replaced glass bottles with plastic ones.
questions.explanation: ガラスを分けて回収し、住民の近くにリサイクル施設を建てたとある。

title: Libraries of things
script: Narrator: Public libraries are known for lending books, but some are now lending a much wider range of items. These so-called libraries of things allow members to borrow tools, camping equipment, musical instruments, and even sewing machines. Supporters say that this saves people money and reduces waste, since many items, such as electric drills, are used only a few times a year. The idea has also helped bring new visitors to libraries. However, libraries must find space to store the items and staff who can check that they are safe and working properly.
translation: 公立図書館は本を貸すことで知られているが、今でははるかに幅広い品を貸す図書館もある。こうした「モノの図書館」では、会員が工具、キャンプ用品、楽器、さらにはミシンまで借りられる。電動ドリルなど多くの品は年に数回しか使われないので、支持者はこれによってお金が節約できごみも減ると言う。この取り組みは図書館に新しい利用者を呼び込むことにもつながった。しかし図書館は、品を保管する場所と、それが安全で正しく動くか確認できる職員を確保しなければならない。

questions.question: Why do supporters like libraries of things?
choices: They save money and reduce waste.
They help libraries sell more books.
They allow people to buy tools cheaply.
They replace traditional book lending.
questions.explanation: 年に数回しか使わない品を借りられるので、お金の節約とごみの削減になると支持者は言っている。

questions.question: What challenge do libraries face?
choices: Finding storage space and staff to check items.
Attracting visitors who want to borrow books.
Paying for members' camping trips.
Teaching members how to play instruments.
questions.explanation: 最後に、保管場所と品の安全を確認できる職員の確保が必要だとある。

title: Night shift workers' health
script: Narrator: Millions of people, including nurses, factory workers, and security guards, regularly work at night. Research has shown that night shift work can have negative effects on health. Because these workers sleep during the day, their body clocks are disrupted, which can lead to problems with digestion and a higher risk of heart disease. To reduce these risks, experts recommend that companies avoid changing workers' schedules too frequently. They also suggest that night workers eat their main meal before their shift starts and keep their bedrooms completely dark when sleeping during the day.
translation: 看護師、工場労働者、警備員など、何百万人もの人が定期的に夜間に働いている。研究によれば、夜勤は健康に悪影響を及ぼしうる。こうした労働者は昼に眠るので体内時計が乱れ、消化の問題や心臓病のリスクの上昇につながりうる。このリスクを減らすため、専門家は企業に勤務スケジュールを頻繁に変えないよう勧めている。また、夜勤の人は勤務開始前に主な食事をとり、昼に眠るときは寝室を真っ暗にするよう提案している。

questions.question: Why can night shift work harm health?
choices: Workers eat too much during their shifts.
It disrupts workers' body clocks.
Workers rarely have time to sleep at all.
Night work is more physically demanding.
questions.explanation: 昼に眠るので体内時計が乱れ、消化の問題や心臓病のリスクにつながると説明されている。

questions.question: What do experts recommend for night workers?
choices: Changing their schedules every week.
Sleeping in a bright room during the day.
Eating their main meal before their shift.
Working only two nights a month.
questions.explanation: 勤務前に主な食事をとり、寝室を真っ暗にするよう勧めている。スケジュールは頻繁に変えないほうがよい。

title: Restoring coral reefs
script: Narrator: Coral reefs around the world are being damaged by rising ocean temperatures. When the water becomes too warm, corals lose the tiny algae that live inside them and turn white, a process known as bleaching. If temperatures do not return to normal, the corals may die. To help reefs recover, scientists are growing small pieces of coral in underwater nurseries and then attaching them to damaged reefs. Some researchers are also breeding corals that can survive in warmer water. However, experts warn that these efforts will not be enough unless global warming is slowed.
translation: 世界中のサンゴ礁が海水温の上昇によって損なわれている。水温が高くなりすぎると、サンゴは体内にすむ小さな藻を失って白くなる。これは白化と呼ばれる。水温が平常に戻らなければサンゴは死ぬこともある。サンゴ礁の回復を助けるため、科学者たちは海中の養殖場で小さなサンゴのかけらを育て、損傷したサンゴ礁に取り付けている。より温かい水でも生きられるサンゴを育種している研究者もいる。しかし、地球温暖化を遅らせなければこうした取り組みだけでは不十分だと専門家は警告している。

questions.question: What causes coral bleaching?
choices: Too many tiny algae living in corals.
Pollution from underwater nurseries.
Fishing boats damaging the reefs.
Water that becomes too warm.
questions.explanation: 水温が高くなりすぎるとサンゴが藻を失って白くなると説明されている。

questions.question: What do experts warn?
choices: Underwater nurseries harm healthy reefs.
Breeding corals is too expensive to continue.
Bleached corals can never recover.
Restoration efforts alone will not be enough.
questions.explanation: 最後に、温暖化を遅らせなければこうした取り組みだけでは不十分だと警告している。

title: Standing desks
script: Narrator: In recent years, standing desks have become popular in offices. Many people believe that sitting for long periods is bad for health, and standing while working seems like an easy solution. However, research suggests that standing for long periods also has disadvantages. It can cause back pain and problems with blood circulation in the legs. Experts say that the most important thing is not to stand all day, but to change positions often. They recommend taking short breaks to walk around every thirty minutes, whether people are sitting or standing.
translation: 近年、立って使う机がオフィスで人気になっている。長時間座ることは健康に悪いと多くの人が考えており、立って仕事をするのは簡単な解決策に思える。しかし研究によると、長時間立つことにも欠点がある。腰痛や脚の血行の問題を引き起こすことがあるのだ。専門家によれば、最も大切なのは一日中立っていることではなく、姿勢をこまめに変えることだ。座っていても立っていても、30分ごとに短い休憩をとって歩き回るよう勧めている。

questions.question: What does research suggest about standing for long periods?
choices: It is the best way to stay healthy at work.
It can cause back pain and circulation problems.
It helps people concentrate for longer.
It has no effect on health.
questions.explanation: 長時間立つことにも欠点があり、腰痛や脚の血行の問題を起こしうるとある。

questions.question: What do experts recommend?
choices: Standing for the whole working day.
Taking short walking breaks regularly.
Using a standing desk only in the morning.
Sitting instead of standing at all times.
questions.explanation: 30分ごとに短い休憩をとって歩き回るよう勧めている。

title: Saving endangered languages
script: Narrator: Linguists estimate that about half of the world's roughly seven thousand languages may disappear by the end of this century. When the last speakers of a language die, knowledge about local history, plants, and traditions can be lost as well. To prevent this, some communities are using technology. They record elderly speakers telling stories and create smartphone apps that teach basic words and phrases. In some places, schools have started offering classes in local languages. However, experts say that a language will only survive if young people use it in their daily lives.
translation: 言語学者の推計では、世界の約7000の言語のおよそ半分が今世紀末までに消える可能性がある。ある言語の最後の話者が亡くなると、地域の歴史、植物、伝統に関する知識も失われうる。これを防ぐため、技術を活用している共同体もある。高齢の話者が物語を語るのを録音し、基本的な単語や表現を教えるスマートフォンのアプリを作っている。地域の言語の授業を始めた学校もある。しかし専門家は、若者が日常生活で使ってこそ言語は生き残ると言う。

questions.question: What can be lost when a language disappears?
choices: The ability to use smartphone apps.
Elderly people's interest in stories.
The number of schools in the region.
Knowledge about local history and traditions.
questions.explanation: 最後の話者が亡くなると、地域の歴史、植物、伝統に関する知識も失われうるとある。

questions.question: According to experts, what is necessary for a language to survive?
choices: It must be taught through smartphone apps.
Young people must use it in daily life.
Elderly speakers must record more stories.
It must become an official national language.
questions.explanation: 最後に、若者が日常生活で使ってこそ言語は生き残ると述べている。

title: Paper straws
script: Narrator: To reduce plastic waste, many restaurants and cafés have replaced plastic straws with paper ones. While customers generally support the idea, many complain that paper straws become soft and fall apart in drinks. Some studies have also found that certain paper straws contain chemicals used to make them waterproof, which may not break down easily in the environment. As a result, some businesses are trying alternatives, such as straws made from rice or bamboo, while others have designed cups with lids that do not require straws at all.
translation: プラスチックごみを減らすため、多くのレストランやカフェがプラスチックのストローを紙のストローに替えた。客は概してこの考えを支持しているが、紙のストローは飲み物の中で柔らかくなって崩れると不満を言う人も多い。紙のストローの中には防水加工のための化学物質を含み、環境中で分解されにくいものがあるという研究もある。その結果、米や竹で作ったストローなどの代替品を試す店や、ストローがまったく要らないふた付きのカップを考案した店もある。

questions.question: What do many customers complain about?
choices: Paper straws are too expensive.
Paper straws become soft in drinks.
Plastic straws are no longer available anywhere.
Paper straws change the taste of drinks.
questions.explanation: 紙のストローは飲み物の中で柔らかくなって崩れると不満を言う人が多いとある。

questions.question: What have some businesses done?
choices: Returned to using plastic straws.
Stopped selling cold drinks.
Asked customers to bring paper straws.
Designed lids that do not need straws.
questions.explanation: 米や竹のストローを試すほか、ストローが要らないふた付きカップを考案した店もあるとある。

title: Walking meetings
script: Narrator: Some companies have started holding walking meetings, in which employees discuss work while walking outside instead of sitting in a conference room. Supporters say that walking increases blood flow to the brain, which can make people more creative. A study at a university found that people produced more original ideas while walking than while sitting. Walking side by side may also make conversations feel less formal, helping employees speak more openly. However, walking meetings are not suitable for every situation, such as when people need to look at documents or take detailed notes.
translation: 会議室に座る代わりに、外を歩きながら仕事について話し合う「ウォーキング会議」を始めた企業がある。支持者によれば、歩くと脳への血流が増え、より創造的になれる。ある大学の研究では、人は座っているときより歩いているときのほうが独創的なアイデアを多く出した。並んで歩くことで会話が堅苦しくなくなり、従業員がより率直に話せるようになるかもしれない。しかし、書類を見たり詳しいメモを取ったりする必要があるときなど、ウォーキング会議がすべての場面に向いているわけではない。

questions.question: What did the university study find?
choices: People took better notes while walking.
Walking meetings were shorter than normal meetings.
People had more original ideas while walking.
Employees preferred meeting in conference rooms.
questions.explanation: 座っているときより歩いているときのほうが独創的なアイデアを多く出したとある。

questions.question: When are walking meetings unsuitable?
choices: When the weather is warm.
When employees want to speak openly.
When only two people are meeting.
When people need to read documents.
questions.explanation: 最後に、書類を見たり詳しいメモを取ったりするときには向かないとある。

title: Tree planting controversy
script: Narrator: Planting trees is often promoted as a simple way to fight climate change, because trees absorb carbon dioxide as they grow. Many companies and governments have announced plans to plant millions or even billions of trees. However, some scientists warn that such projects can cause harm if they are not carefully planned. For example, planting trees on natural grasslands can destroy habitats for animals and plants that depend on open land. In addition, many young trees die because no one takes care of them after planting. Experts say that protecting existing forests is often more effective than planting new ones.
translation: 木は成長するにつれて二酸化炭素を吸収するので、植林は気候変動と戦う簡単な方法としてよく宣伝される。多くの企業や政府が何百万本、何十億本もの木を植える計画を発表している。しかし、慎重に計画しなければこうした事業は害をもたらしうると警告する科学者もいる。例えば、自然の草原に木を植えると、開けた土地に頼る動植物のすみかを壊してしまう。さらに、植えた後に世話をする人がいないため、多くの若木が枯れる。専門家によれば、新しい木を植えるより既存の森林を守るほうが効果的なことが多い。

questions.question: What problem can planting trees on grasslands cause?
choices: It can destroy habitats for some animals and plants.
It increases the amount of carbon dioxide.
It makes the soil too wet for farming.
It attracts too many tourists.
questions.explanation: 自然の草原に木を植えると、開けた土地に頼る動植物のすみかを壊してしまうとある。

questions.question: What do experts say is often more effective?
choices: Planting billions of trees quickly.
Planting trees only on grasslands.
Cutting down old trees to plant new ones.
Protecting forests that already exist.
questions.explanation: 最後に、既存の森林を守るほうが効果的なことが多いと述べている。

title: Smart cities and privacy
script: Narrator: Around the world, cities are using sensors and data to improve public services. These so-called smart cities can adjust traffic lights based on the number of cars, monitor air pollution, and tell residents when the next bus will arrive. Supporters say that such technology can make cities more efficient and reduce energy use. However, critics are concerned about privacy. Cameras and sensors may collect large amounts of information about people's movements, and residents often do not know how this data is stored or used. Some cities have responded by creating clear rules about what data can be collected.
translation: 世界中の都市が、公共サービスを改善するためにセンサーやデータを活用している。こうした「スマートシティ」では、車の数に応じて信号を調整し、大気汚染を監視し、次のバスがいつ来るかを住民に知らせることができる。支持者は、こうした技術で都市がより効率的になりエネルギー使用も減ると言う。しかし批判する人はプライバシーを懸念している。カメラやセンサーは人々の移動について大量の情報を集める可能性があり、住民はそのデータがどう保存され使われるかを知らないことが多い。どのデータを集めてよいかについて明確な規則を作って対応した都市もある。

questions.question: What is one thing smart cities can do?
choices: Adjust traffic lights according to traffic.
Provide free buses for all residents.
Stop all air pollution in the city.
Reduce the number of cars to zero.
questions.explanation: 車の数に応じて信号を調整できると述べている。

questions.question: How have some cities responded to privacy concerns?
choices: By removing all cameras from the streets.
By selling residents' data to companies.
By making clear rules about data collection.
By stopping the use of sensors completely.
questions.explanation: 最後に、どのデータを集めてよいかについて明確な規則を作ったとある。
